name: MonarchPhoneInput
title: PhoneInput
wrapsNative: TextField with .keyboardType(.phonePad) and .textContentType(.telephoneNumber), beside a Button that opens MonarchPhoneCountrySelect's searchable country list (a .sheet with a List and .searchable)
summary: A phone number field with a country calling code button, which writes one E.164 value such as +442079460958.
whenToUse: Whenever a form asks for a phone number that has to be dialled or texted from anywhere: sign-up, delivery contact, two-step verification.
whenNotToUse: Not for a calling code on its own; use MonarchPhoneCountrySelect. Not for an extension or an internal short number; use MonarchTextField with .keyboardType(.phonePad).
api: init(_ label: String, value: Binding<String?>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, defaultCountry: String = "US", countries: [String]? = nil, preferred: [String] = [], locale: Locale? = nil, showsFlags: Bool = true, isRequired: Bool = false, labels: MonarchPhoneInputLabels = MonarchPhoneInputLabels(), onCountryChange: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)
static func toE164(dialCode: String, national: String, country: String? = nil) -> String?
static func isValidE164(_ value: String) -> Bool
static func parse(_ phone: String, preferred: String? = nil) -> MonarchPhoneInputDetails?
struct MonarchPhoneInputDetails: Sendable, Hashable { let country: String; let dialCode: String; let national: String; init(country: String, dialCode: String, national: String) }

struct MonarchPhoneInputLabels: Sendable { init(country: String? = nil, invalid: String? = nil, countrySelect: MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels = MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels(), field: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It names the number field.

options.name: value
options.description: The number in E.164, or nil when empty. Any international form (+44 20 7946 0958, 0044…) is read when it is set.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder text in the number field while it is empty.

options.name: error
options.description: An error from the app, shown with an icon and announced. The component's own incomplete-number message takes its place while it shows.

options.name: defaultCountry
options.description: The ISO code of the country when the value does not give one. Read once, when the view is created.

options.name: countries
options.description: Limits the country list to these ISO codes. nil lists every country in MonarchPhoneCountry.all.

options.name: preferred
options.description: ISO codes listed first in the country list under Suggested.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the country names in the list and the spoken value. The environment's locale when nil.

options.name: showsFlags
options.description: Shows the flag on the country button and in the list.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds Required to the hint.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Country code, Enter a complete phone number., the country list strings and the spoken Required and error prefix.

options.name: onCountryChange
options.description: Receives the ISO code when the country changes, from the list, a pasted number or a shared calling code.

states.name: empty
states.description: The number field shows the prompt in the subtle text colour; the button shows the default country's flag and calling code.

states.name: typing
states.description: The value is not changed on each keystroke; a pasted full international number moves to its country at once and keeps the national digits.

states.name: committed
states.description: When the field loses focus, Return is pressed or the country changes, a valid number is written as E.164 and the field shows its national digits.

states.name: invalid
states.description: A number outside 8 to 15 digits, or an international number with no known calling code, keeps its text, is not written, and shows Enter a complete phone number. with an icon and a danger border.

states.name: error
states.description: An app error shows under the row with an icon, and both borders take the danger colour.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Both parts take the disabled fill, border and text colours and do not respond.

states.name: accessibility sizes
states.description: At the accessibility text sizes the country button sits above the number field instead of beside it.

appearance: The button and the field are separate bordered controls on the surface fill with the input border, as MonarchTextField; an error turns both borders to the strong danger colour. The calling code and number use the default text colour, the chevron the muted secondary colour. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows the country select and the input in one row with a hidden form input; iOS has no form submission, so the binding is the value. The country list is the one MonarchPhoneCountrySelect shows, opened from a compact flag and calling code button, because the full combobox field does not fit beside a number on a phone. The web's Escape to restore the last value has no counterpart on the phone pad. The web's sm, md and lg control sizes are not offered: iOS fields have one size that grows with Dynamic Type. Android has no PhoneInput yet; the names follow the web and the plan (MonarchPhoneInput). The web reports details in onValueChange; iOS gives MonarchPhoneInput.parse(_:preferred:) and onCountryChange.
accessibility: The visible label is hidden from VoiceOver and given to the number field, whose value is the typed number.
The field's hint is the error (read as Error: …), the help text and Required, each when present; a new error is announced.
The country button is named Country code and its value is the country and calling code, such as Portugal (+351), in the chosen language.
Errors are an icon and text and a border, not colour alone.
The number field and the button are laid out left to right in right-to-left languages, as phone numbers are written.
The button and the field are at least 44 points high; at the accessibility text sizes they stack.
The country list's rows are buttons with the selected trait and a check mark on the current country.
edgeCases: One trunk 0 is dropped (020 7946 0958 under +44 is +442079460958), except for Italy, San Marino and Vatican City.
Countries sharing a calling code are resolved from the number: 242 555 0100 typed under US is written as +12425550100 and the country moves to the Bahamas.
Digits typed in Arabic-Indic, Persian or full-width forms, and bidirectional marks from pasted text, are read.
A value set by the app that has no known calling code is shown as digits under the current country.
Clearing the field and leaving it writes nil; it is not an error. Use error to require a number.
The phone pad has no Return key, so the value is written when focus leaves the field; read the binding after focus moves, for example on submit of the form.

examples.title: In a Field with suggested countries
examples.webExample: In a Field with suggested countries
examples.code:
MonarchPhoneInput(
    "Phone",
    value: $phone,
    helper: "Stored as" + " " + (phone ?? "nothing yet") + ".",
    preferred: ["GB", "US", "IN"]
)

examples.title: A required number in another default country
examples.setup:
@State private var phone: String?
@State private var country = "PT"
examples.code:
MonarchPhoneInput(
    "Work phone",
    value: $phone,
    prompt: "912 345 678",
    defaultCountry: "PT",
    isRequired: true,
    onCountryChange: { country = $0 }
)
